text:
Sam: heads up — we've got ~40 pods pending in eu-west-1 with Insufficient gpu resources. noticed after the night deploy :frowning:
Maya: ugh. are these fractional-gpu requests or full-GPU? any pattern from the pod specs?
Sam: mostly full GPUs, but mixed flavors. some request nvidia.com/gpu=1, others request nvidia.com/gpu=2. many are node-affinity'd to nodepool-gpu-mix.
Jordan: that nodepool has A100 and A10 nodes in same pool (legacy reason). packing across different gpu-count labels is causing fragmentation.
Lee: exactly — autoscaler won't split flavors. if a pod needs 2 GPUs and it lands on A10 nodes with 1 GPU each available, it stays pending.
Ana: can we force pod to tolerate taints and prefer A100? or better: split into separate nodepools by GPU SKU and GPU count (1g,2g)?
Sam: short-term patch: I changed the pod's nodeAffinity to prefer nodes with label gpu.count=2 for the largest jobs. resubmitted a few, they bound.
Maya: can you paste the pending pod describe? curious if scheduler preemption+binpacking could have helped.
Sam: sure — here's the describe for one pending pod:
```
Name:         trainer-92b
Namespace:    ml-prod
Status:       Pending
Conditions:   Type=PodScheduled Status=False Reason=Unschedulable
Message:      0/12 nodes are available: 5 node(s) had taint {gpu-type: A100}, 4 node(s) had insufficient gpu, 3 node(s) had unrelated taints.
```
Jordan: scheduler thinks some nodes have taint gpu-type:A100 (we applied that when we consolidated dedicated pools). pods without toleration get rejected.
Lee: autoscaler logs show scale-up events but they target the wrong GPU flavor because of mixed labels. we need scale-to-zero disabled on the 2g pool maybe.
Ana: medium-term: split nodepools by sku and by gpu-count. also make autoscaler Policy: prefer largest-fit for multi-gpu requests. that should reduce cross-flavor fragmentation.
Maya: cost question — splitting pools increases idle costs if we keep reserves. can Optimize recommend right target sizes per cluster based on historical demand?
Sam: yes, I can run a 7-day query on pod GPU requests and give a suggested reserved capacity per pool. quick numbers show 30% of GPU jobs are 2+ GPUs.
k8s-bot: [alert] cluster-autoscaler: scale-up activity triggered for nodepool-gpu-2g-eu-west-1 (requested 4 nodes)
Jordan: once scale-up finishes, we should also run a gentle rollout: cordon a mixed node and drain small jobs so binpacking frees larger contiguous GPUs.
Lee: FYI, there's also an issue where GKE spot preemption spikes cause tiny gaps across nodes, worsening fragmentation. we should enable better preemption handling in the scheduler extender.
Ana: for next sprint proposal: 1) split gpu nodepools by SKU and gpu-count labels, 2) adjust autoscaler priorities, 3) add admission webhook to reject pods that would create impossible packing (like request 2g with affinity only to 1g nodes), 4) run cost forecast for reserved capacity.
Maya: +1. also add a monitoring widget: "gpu fragmentation ratio" (percent of available GPUs unusable due to binpacking mismatch).
Sam: I'll open an RFC doc and link it. In the meantime I'll keep manually preferring gpu.count=2 for the 2g jobs.
Jordan: thanks — looping in @Ana for the autoscaler policy change and @Lee for scheduling extender work.
Lee: will start a spike on the extender next week.
Ana: I'll draft the cost impact numbers and expected savings if we reduce fragmentation by 20-30%.
Sam: awesome. if anyone sees more pending pods, ping me.
Maya: thanks Sam :thumbsup:
__note: No title field included per agents.md requirement. Thread is a single continuous string with messages in chronological order.
